ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows triangle ABC, with B on the left, C at the upper right, A at the lower right, and point J located inside the triangle. In the figure, J is connected to the sides and vertices of the triangle, and ∠ABJ = 34° and ∠BCJ = 32° are labeled. Pink right-angle marks show that there are perpendiculars from J to each side, matching an incenter-related structure. Reasoning: Given that J is the incenter of triangle ABC, BJ, CJ, and AJ respectively bisect ∠B, ∠C, and ∠A. Therefore ∠ABC = 2 × 34° = 68°, and ∠BCA = 2 × 32° = 64°. By the sum of the interior angles of a triangle, ∠BAC = 180° − 68° − 64° = 48°. Also because AJ bisects ∠A, ∠JAC = 48° ÷ 2 = 24°.

method.method_draft: From the image, identify triangle ABC with point J inside; the marked 34° angle is ∠ABJ, and the marked 32° angle is ∠BCJ. From the text, use that J is the incenter, so BJ, CJ, and AJ are angle bisectors of triangle ABC. Therefore ∠ABC = 2·34° = 68° and ∠BCA = 2·32° = 64°. Use the triangle angle sum to get ∠BAC = 180° − 68° − 64° = 48°. Since AJ also bisects angle A, ∠JAC = 48°/2 = 24°.
